memories.content: The rear entrance on the third floor of the Main Building connects directly to the pedestrian route leading to the Central Library.
With your back to the main entrance, Outdoor Parking Lot A is on the left.
With your back to the main entrance, the West Complex is on the left.
With your back to the main entrance, the Humanities Building is on the right.
The Student Centre is behind the Central Library.
The Outdoor Parking Lot A–Main Building–Central Library route is usually short.
The Outdoor Parking Lot A–Main Building–Central Library route has a long indoor section.
The route from Outdoor Parking Lot C through the Student Centre accessible entrance to the west entrance of the Central Library does not pass through the Main Building.
In summer, students prefer the air-conditioned indoor route from the first to the third floor of the Main Building over the outdoor route.
Recommend only routes that are currently confirmed to be open.
Explain the distinction between the standard shortest route and the accessible route.
The route guidance agent can compare routes using stored geographic information.
The route guidance agent cannot check congestion in real time.
The route guidance agent cannot check for movable obstacles.
The route guidance agent cannot check in real time for newly installed temporary signs or movable control barriers at the time of inquiry.
There is no continuous accessible route that a wheelchair can use in the direction of the stairs on the right side of the Main Building.
The detour from the stairs on the right side of the Main Building to the Student Centre is long.
Mobility support companions prefer the indoor route through the Main Building to the Central Library because it is less affected by weather.
The public campus map shows building entrances and pedestrian paths between buildings.
The public campus map separately marks step-free accessible routes.
The pedestrian path in front of the Main Building's main entrance has a sign indicating the direction of the accessible route.
A step-free pedestrian path runs from Outdoor Parking Lot C to the Student Centre accessible entrance.
An accessible route runs from the Student Centre to the west entrance of the Central Library.
There is an above-ground pedestrian path from the West Complex to the Main Building's main entrance.
The pedestrian path from the Humanities Building to the Main Building's main entrance passes in front of the stairs on the right side of the Main Building.
Using the elevator from the first-floor lobby of the Main Building provides step-free access to the level of the third-floor rear entrance.
The escalator route in the Main Building includes a section where stairs cannot be avoided.
When step-free travel is required, direct people to the elevator route rather than the escalator route.
The elevator closest to the Main Building's main entrance is inside the first-floor lobby.
The above-ground route between the Main Building and the Central Library has a rest bench midway.
Solbit Plaza is between the Main Building's main entrance and the West Complex.
When it rains or snows, travel time on sloped outdoor pedestrian paths may be longer than usual.
Snow removal personnel judge that when it snows, major accessible routes must be cleared before other pedestrian paths.
Students going to the library after parking prefer the familiar, short Outdoor Parking Lot A–Main Building–Central Library route.
During class change times, pedestrian traffic increases between the third floor of the Main Building and the Central Library.
First-time visitors find directions based on visible facilities easier to understand than directions based on building numbers.
Because of the sloped terrain, first-time visitors sometimes confuse the levels of the Main Building's first-floor main entrance and third-floor rear entrance.
Delivery drivers consider designated service routes that do not mix with pedestrians more predictable and safer.
The route guidance agent cannot check on-site congestion in real time and can compare posted detours to identify routes with fewer branches.
The route guidance agent can distinguish stair routes from elevator routes on the public map.
The route guidance agent cannot measure on-site pedestrian traffic at the time of inquiry.
The route guidance agent cannot guarantee an individual user's travel time.
Check the current notice for the destination entrance before giving directions.
Do not recommend staff-only passages as detours to general users.
If the shortest route has stairs, also present an available accessible route.
In an emergency, instruct people to follow on-site evacuation signs and safety personnel's directions rather than general wayfinding guidance.
A pedestrian path from the West Gate stop to the Main Building's main entrance runs through Solbit Plaza.
There is a step-free route from the shuttle stop in front of the Student Centre to the west entrance of the Central Library.
Bicycle users dismount at the designated rack on the edge of Solbit Plaza and proceed on foot.
Do not suggest informal shortcuts that are not on the public map as default routes.
Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, the underground parking garage cannot be used for general parking.
Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, the pedestrian entrance door to the underground parking garage is kept locked.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, instruct staff to use a physical access card to pass through the locked pedestrian entrance door to the underground parking garage.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: Instruct construction/facilities personnel to access the underground parking garage through the controlled on-site access procedure that has been approved.
Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: The stairs from the Main Building down to the underground parking garage are closed to all users.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: The underground parking garage is used as a temporary storage area for construction materials.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: After the clear-out, personal items left in the underground parking garage were moved to the lost and found center.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: Outdoor Parking Lot A connected to the Main Building is closed during the construction period.
Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, Outdoor Parking Lot C operates as a temporary alternative parking lot for vehicles visiting the Main Building.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: Outdoor Parking Lot A is planned to reopen immediately after construction on the Main Building ends.
Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, the sloped access road connecting Outdoor Parking Lot A and the Main Building underground parking garage is blocked.

Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: Based on posted information, the parking guidance agent may explain the closures of the underground parking garage and Outdoor Parking Lot A and the alternative use of Outdoor Parking Lot C during the construction period.

Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, the parking guidance agent may explain the location of Outdoor Parking Lot C but cannot check or guarantee available spaces at the time of an inquiry.

Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: A visitor accustomed to parking at the Main Building may expect to be able to enter the underground parking garage or Outdoor Parking Lot A during the construction period, drive as far as the closed access road, and then search again for Outdoor Parking Lot C.

Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: Delivery drivers and external maintenance contractors accustomed to unloading in Outdoor Parking Lot A may approach the same point during the construction period and then reconfirm the delivery time or unloading location at the control line.

analysis.overview: Both frames support status-aware guidance, while construction temporarily changes familiar parking, access, and delivery patterns. The reference primarily covers campus wayfinding, accessibility, route characteristics, and agent limits; the compared frame adds underground-garage restrictions, temporary parking operations, storage, and lost-property handling.

relations.reason: The construction-period condition preserves the ordinary route characteristics and preferences while explaining the temporary closure, blocked access road, alternative parking, and likely visitor misdirection.
relations.summary: A familiar, generally short route from Outdoor Parking Lot A through the Main Building is unavailable during construction, when Lot C serves as the alternative; Lot A is planned to reopen afterward.

relations.reason: These claims jointly govern status-aware guidance without contradiction: posted information supports explanations, while current verification and sensing limits qualify its use.
relations.summary: Guidance may explain posted construction closures, subject to checking current entrance notices and recognizing that newly installed temporary controls may not be visible to the agent.

relations.reason: Explicit user-role conditions distinguish prohibited public routing from authorized card or controlled-procedure access.
relations.summary: The locked underground-garage pedestrian entrance is not a general-user detour, while authorized staff and construction or facilities personnel may use approved controlled access.

relations.reason: The construction condition adds a temporary delivery-handling case without displacing the general safety preference.
relations.summary: Delivery users generally favor designated routes separated from pedestrians, while construction may bring drivers and contractors to a control line where timing or unloading must be reconfirmed.

reports.both: Guidance may communicate posted closures, but current entrance status and unseen temporary controls remain important qualifications.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame adds underground-garage closure and storage use, closed garage stairs, lost-property handling, and inability to confirm live parking capacity.
reports.differences: Construction redirects familiar Lot A users to Lot C, distinguishes authorized controlled access from public routes, and changes delivery handling at the control line.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers campus geography, pedestrian and accessible routes, map features, weather and traffic effects, user preferences, safety rules, and wayfinding-agent limits.
